programme: BTG2 and KLF14 both target SPHK1, the enzyme that generates sphingosine-1-phosphate (S1P); BTG2 additionally targets the antioxidant enzymes SOD1, SOD2 and CAT and the cell-cycle genes CCND1/HRAS, while KLF14 also targets TGFBR2 and FGFR1. TGIF1 (targeting TGFB1, SERPINE1, CDKN1A) reinforces the TGF-β/p21 arm that KLF14's TGFBR2 target feeds into, and MEF2D/EGR4 (targeting CDKN1A, GADD45A, GADD45B, ATM, FOS, TNF, IL2) supply the stress-inducible, immediate-early apoptosis-versus-survival switch this axis converges on.
role_in_a: In melanoma, KLF14-SLC7A11 signalling protects cells from ferroptosis and BTG2 targets a mitochondrial/oxidative-stress gene set, together supporting tumour-cell survival under oxidative and therapy-induced stress.
role_in_b: In stroke, KLF14 variants associate with ischemic stroke risk and KLF14-linked exosomal signalling dampens post-ischemic inflammation; MEF2D drives anti-apoptotic post-conditioning and an oxidative-stress/inflammation pathway after cerebral ischemia; EGR4 supports neuronal regeneration after ischemic injury; BTG2 tracks as an inflammatory biomarker in ischemic stroke.
shared_axis: Melanoma cells under oxidative/therapeutic stress and neurovascular cells under ischemia-reperfusion stress both appear to route the decision between apoptosis and survival through SPHK1-generated S1P coupled to an antioxidant/TGF-β/p21 stress-response circuit; the two diseases converge on this module because it is a generic cell-stress-survival system, engaged separately by tumour-intrinsic oxidative stress in one and vascular ischemia in the other, not because of any documented disease-to-disease link.
reasoning: No source states that melanoma and stroke share this axis, so this is not established. But four of the five carrying factors are independently placed by name in at least one disease (BTG2 and KLF14 in both), and the module — S1P/SPHK1 plus an antioxidant and TGF-β/p21 stress-response circuit — is directly nameable from the given target lists rather than reached for. That combination of independent placement and a self-evident mechanism from the record itself is why this sits at 'supported / strong' rather than 'unexpected' or 'moderate'.
support: PMID 37869567 — BTG2 tied to mitochondria-related, oxidative-stress targets in melanoma cells (quercetin study); PMID 40119397 — BTG2 as an inflammatory-response biomarker in ischemic stroke; PMID 39518098 — KLF14-SLC7A11 signalling protects mucosal melanoma from ferroptosis; PMID 41676086 — KLF14 among gene variants associated with ischemic stroke in an exome cohort; PMID 38756375 — KLF14-linked exosomal signalling reduces post-ischemic inflammation; PMID 33621420 — MEF2D mediates anti-apoptotic effect of post-conditioning after cerebral ischemia; PMID 32311345 — MEF2D-HDAC5/ND6 pathway in oxidative stress and inflammation after stroke; PMID 40320842 — EGR4 identified as a target for neuronal regeneration after ischemic stroke. TGIF1 has no direct disease evidence in the record; its role here rests on target overlap (TGFB1/SERPINE1/CDKN1A) with KLF14 and MEF2D, not on retrieved papers.
how_to_falsify: Knock down or pharmacologically inhibit SPHK1 (or BTG2/KLF14 individually) in parallel in (1) a melanoma line under ferroptotic/oxidative stress and (2) a neuronal or endothelial ischemia-reperfusion model. If the shared axis is real, both should show concordant shifts in survival — reduced ferroptosis resistance in melanoma and worse post-ischemic apoptosis/infarct extent in the stroke model. If the intervention changes outcome in only one system, the shared-module claim fails.
caveats: Blood and skin share no anatomy, so any account here must rest on a generic stress-survival programme rather than shared tissue biology — this is reflected in the verdict of 'supported' rather than 'established'. The 27 patient-group comparisons rest on only 2 independent cohort pairs, limiting how much the concordance counts can be trusted as replication. GTF3A topped concordance (25/27) but was excluded: its inferred target set (VEGFA, CXCL8, TNF, PLAU, ADM, STAT1) does not match its canonical role as a Pol III/5S-rRNA transcription factor, and no disease evidence exists for it in either condition, so it looks like network-inference noise rather than an omission. TEAD2, HEYL, NPAS2, ZNF281, HOXD1 and RBCK1 were also left out of the programme — TEAD2 has real melanoma-specific drug-resistance evidence but no mechanistic link to the SPHK1/stress axis or to stroke, and the rest have neither. The single-view exclusions (FOXK2, HLX, NSD2, E2F7, RERE, SALL4, ZNF8) and tissue-generic exclusions (HLX, SMAD3, VDR, STAT5A/B, BCL3, GLI1, ETS1, SREBF2, IRF4, NFATC1, CREB5) confirm this account is not built on one subgroup or on generic blood/immune regulators.
